sentences.text: The facts of the case are as under:
The deceased is the legally wedded wife of the accused and their marriage was solemnized on 24.04.2016.
At the time of marriage, the accused  3 S.C.No.368/2018 demanded and received 9 thola gold as dowry.
Thereafter, the accused started to torture the deceased and demanded additional dowry of Rs.5 Lakh.

On 15.09.2017 in House No.1312, 12 th Cross, 1st Stage,
Chandra Layout, the accused abused the deceased in filthy language and restrained her from talking with anybody, assaulted with hands and confined in the house.
On the same day, between 11.00a.m and 12.00 noon, the wife of the accused had committed suicide by hanging.
The accused is responsible for her death.
Hence, this charge sheet.
3. Accused is on bail.
4. Charge framed.
Accused has denied the charge and claimed to be tried.
5. To prove the case, the prosecution has examined its witnesses as P.W.1 to P.W.13.
The  4 S.C.No.368/2018 documents are marked as Ex.P.1 to P.28 and M.O.1 to M.O.9.
The learned prosecutor has requested to summon C.W. 2 to C.W.4, C.W.7 to C.W.11, C.W.22 to C.W.36, C.W.38 to C.W.45.

The material witnesses State Of Karnataka vs Vijaykumar Math on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151253642/

6. The statement of the accused U/s.313 of Cr.P.C recorded.
The accused has denied the incriminating evidence and not chosen to lead defence evidence.
7. Heard both.

8. The points that arise for my consideration are:
 1.
Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that at the time of his marriage with the deceased, the accused demanded and received 9 thola gold as dowry and thereby committed the offence punishable U/sec.3 of D.P. Act?

2. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that after the marriage, the accused demanded additional dowry of Rs.5,00,000/- and thereby committed the offence punishable U/sec.4 of D.P.Act ?

3. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that since from the date of marriage,
the accused used to harass the deceased, demanded additional dowry of Rs.5 Lakh, treated her with physical and mental cruelty and thereby committed the offence punishable U/sec.498A of IPC?

4. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that without bearing the dowry harassment and cruelty, on 15.09.2017 between 11.00a.m and 12.00 noon at House No.1312, 12 th Cross, 1st Stage, Chandra Layout, the wife of the accused had committed suicide by hanging and the accused is responsible for her death and thereby committed the offence punishable U/sec.304B of IPC?
5. What order?

9. My findings on the above points are as hereunder:
Point No.1 to 4 : In the Negative Point No.5 : As per final order for the following:
:R E A S O N S:
10. Points No.1 to 4 : All the points involve common discussion.
C.W.1 is a father of the deceased and he is a complainant.
He deposed as P.W.1.
He has denied the complaint averments.
According to him, the accused never demanded and received dowry.

He has stated that, his daughter was in good State Of Karnataka vs Vijaykumar Math on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151253642/

12.

He has stated that, his elder sister had committed suicide without bearing the severe stomach pain.
He has denied the facts of the case and turned hostile.
During the course of his cross- examination by the prosecutor, he has denied the contents of the statement said to have been recorded by the Thasildar.

It is marked as Ex.P.7.
13.
C.W.5 & C.W.6 have been examined as P.W.4 & P.W.5.
According to the prosecution, they are mahazar witnesses.
They identified their signature on mahazar and does not know the contents.
Both have deposed their ignorance about the seizure of articles.
Mahazar is marked as Ex.P.8.
At the time of cross- examination by the prosecutor, both have denied the contents of Ex.P.8 and seizure of broken bolt and Samsung J2 mobile phone.

They are marked as M.O.1 and M.O.2.
14.

She is the younger sister of the deceased.

At the time of cross-examination by the prosecutor, he has has denied the contents of the statement marked as per Ex.P.11.

23.

24. It is worth to note that the accused himself had appeared before the complainant police and intimated the death of his wife.
C.W.1 and other relatives are turned hostile.
The alleged panch witnesses have failed to support the prosecution.
The parents, brother, sister and close relatives of C.W.1 have clearly stated that, the deceased was suffering from stomach pain.
25. Admittedly, there is no death note.

There was no anti- mortem injuries except ligature mark of hanging.

26. Point No.5:

With these discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
O RDE R Acting under Section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under sec.498A, 304B of Indian Penal Code and Sec.3 & 4 of D.P.Act.
The bail bond executed by the accused and the surety bond shall stand cancelled.
M.O.1, M.O.3 to M.O.9 are worthless and shall be destroyed after appeal period.
M.O.2 to be confiscated to State after appeal period.
